title: Air Force Project Blue Book
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Air Force Project Blue Book, about 1947-1968 at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: The Air Force even established its own UFO investigation program called Operation Blue Book.
the blue book history is edward j rupelt was sort of running blue book he was an air force general and he seemed pretty open-minded to the phenomena being real
tellings.difference: This telling names Edward Ruppelt as running Blue Book in the early 1950s and calls him an Air Force general, and it says he seemed open-minded to the phenomena being real, details the story lacks.
tellings.link_reason: Both tellings are about the US Air Force's Project Blue Book UFO investigation program, told by the same host. This telling describes the program through the person running it rather than through a separate incident inside it.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the US Air Force once set up its own UFO investigation programme, which he calls Operation Blue Book, running from the late 1940s through the 1960s. In one telling he says it was run for a time by Edward J. Ruppelt, whom he calls an Air Force general, and who he says seemed fairly open to the idea that the sightings were real. It matters because it would mean the military itself once took the question seriously.
